profile.headline: Software Manager at Intuitive Surgical
profile.summary: My name is pronounced muh-sepp jack-sun uh-toe-gee. While it is not necessarily preferred, I often go by the nickname Moss. I am currently a software engineer for Intuitive Surgical. I enjoy taking on new endeavors, challenging myself, and gaining new perspectives from others.  In my spare time I enjoy programming, games, listening to music and doing most anything active.  I have played soccer since I was five years old and it has been an instrumental part of my life.  Enough about me, let's connect :)

positions.title: Software Engineer Technical Lead
positions.description: Member of field service applications software team responsible for developing laptop apps/tools for testing da Vinci systems. I am the primary contributor and subject matter expert for field service software for one of the da Vinci products. Technical experience includes inter-process communication design, test workflow design, and various coding/documentation standards. Primary languages used are Python, MATLAB, with some light HTML/JS/CSS. Both Subversion and Git used for version control, JIRA for issue tracking, and Confluence for documentation. Other experience includes working in highly cross-functional teams, drafting requirements and formal test protocols, and working in access and change control systems.

positions.title: Software Enginner
positions.description: Solely responsible for software application used for real-time imaging of the eye during surgery (via optical coherence tomography), as well as post-operative viewing and analysis.  Non-technical experience includes presenting software features to end-users, responding to feature requests and bug fixes, and issue tracking via Bitbucket and Trello.  Technical experience includes building GUI applications, GPU-programming  (both general purpose and image rendering) using CUDA, hardware-software integration, and OpenGL.  Visual Studio (C++), Qt, and Git used for development.  Major completed projects include: creation of a heads up display for surgeons intraoperatively,  improved/added ability to control motorized stages, simplified and intuitive user interface for clinical use, and addition of new laser scan patterns.  Co-author on multiple papers.

positions.title: Software Engineering Intern
positions.description: Backend developer for an ERP system. Languages used were Go and SQL. Heroku used to launch an API server and postgres database was implemented. Involved in the whole process of adding features, including planning, implementation, and testing. Used GitHub for version control and PivotalTracker to track and measure progress.

projects.title: Cervical Cancer Screening
projects.description: Led design and implementation of a program for detecting dysplastic cervices based off of clinical cervix images. Algorithm involved creating a support vector machine via metrics obtained from the color content of training images. Written in Python with robust unit testing, Sphinx documentation, and continuous integration.

projects.title: BB-nate
projects.description: As part of a graduate design course, partnered with Duke Hospital's NICU department, my team and I developed a prototype of a device designed to determine a neonate's bone mineral density noninvasively. This project heavily involved the four major aspects that go into developing a (medical) device: software, electrical hardware, physical hardware, & testing. Each team member was responsible for leading one of the four aspects and constant collaboration was necessary for completion. I was responsible for leading software, therefore defining the microcontroller the device would use and how it should connect to the electrical hardware, as well as the programming language and algorithm to be implemented. Git was used for version contorl.
